A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaQN work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and can be matched across the added subsections and repagination.

before.justification: V2 reports original LunarLander, MuJoCo, and Atari experiments, including baseline comparisons, ablations, and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments, revises Figure 4 results, and adds estimates of the experiments’ carbon emissions.

M1.justification: AdaDQN, AdaSAC, target selection, behavioral policies, and the infinite-space evolutionary extension are retained. The new mathematical formulation and tabular analysis do not change the implemented algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use LunarLander, the same six MuJoCo environments, and the same Atari game sets for finite-space, infinite-space, and discount-factor experiments. The extended random-search curve remains within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same individual DQN/SAC configurations, random and grid search, RandDQN/RandSAC, SEARL, DEHB, and Meta-gradient DQN. Newly cited theoretical works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 4 extends the reported finite-space random-search comparison from approximately 0.5 million to 8 million cumulative environment steps; Appendix B.2 describes sequential-trial postprocessing. Tables 1–4 retain their settings. Newly disclosed replay-data reuse for infinite-space baselines does not establish a change in their implementation.

E4.justification: The new Carbon Impact section adds an environmental-cost analysis using two estimation tools. Existing behavioral-policy and hyperparameter ablations, case studies, and Appendix C’s time and memory analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 newly discloses Monte Carlo sampling of hyperparameter sequences to estimate random-search performance. The 20/9/5 seed counts and 95% stratified-bootstrap confidence-interval practice remain unchanged; revised band values in Figure 4 are result changes.

E6.justification: Figure 4 revises the grid-search aggregate, extends random-search trajectories, and updates confidence bands. These are revised baseline summaries, not an AdaSAC performance gain. V3 also reports 1.30–1.53 tonnes of CO2 equivalent; the other experimental figures retain their results.

T1.justification: V3 adds the bilevel hyperparameter formulation in Equation (2) and Appendix A.1’s argument for almost-sure tabular convergence, extending Generalized Q-learning to history-dependent target selection. This substantially expands the theory beyond the retained approximation-error result and proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about adaptive shared targets, sample efficiency, performance, robustness, and theoretical soundness. The introduction clarifies the existing focus on online hyperparameter adaptation.

C2.justification: The carbon analysis explicitly limits its estimates to computations producing the reported figures, excluding preliminary studies, and contextualizes them against an annual per-person carbon budget. Existing explanations of performance and Section 6’s limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 supplies a code-repository URL, identifies the Atari codebase’s provenance, and adds Appendix B.2’s baseline aggregation and replay-reuse details. These improve documentation without establishing corresponding implementation changes. The earlier acceptance-contingent code footnote remains.

R1.justification: V3 adds Lan et al. (2020) for the convergence framework, Vincent et al. (2025) for implementation provenance, and three carbon-accounting references. The principal AutoRL positioning and related-work comparisons remain stable.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the introduction, preliminaries, and experimental reporting. New convergence and evaluation-protocol subsections, acknowledgments, and carbon-impact text extend the document while preserving its main narrative and section order.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reduced in size, Figure 9 moves relative to the experimental-setup text, and citation colors, spacing, and a table caption change. The existing figure and table inventory and overall display structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.2, the code link, and extended baseline reporting improve transparency. However, Appendix A.1’s new convergence argument asserts an inequality bounding differences between independently selected ensemble members by the distance between ensembles. With identical ensembles but unequal selected members, that distance is zero while the selected values can differ. This substantive proof gap accompanies the documentation gains, leaving their net effect on overall quality uncertain.
